fluff.name: Expert
entries: Experts rely on cunning, stealth, and their foes' vulnerabilities to get the upper hand in any situation. They have a knack for finding the solution to just about any problem. A few even learn magical tricks to supplement their other abilities. Many Experts focus on stealth and deception, while others refine skills that help them in a dungeon environment, such as climbing, finding and disarming traps, and opening locks.
In combat, Experts prioritize subtle strikes over brute strength. They would rather make one precise strike than wear an opponent down with a barrage of blows.

Some Experts began their careers as criminals, while others used their cunning to fight crime. Whatever an Expert's relation to the law, no common criminal or officer of the law can match the subtle brilliance of the greatest Experts.

fluff.name: Shaman
entries: Nature is a powerful force containing a myriad of mysterious magics. Shamans have the ability - learned, intuited, or innate - to act as a conduit for that natural magic.
Shamans channel ancient rites in the form of runes, summon elemental spirits, and evoke powerful elemental magic to manipulate their enemies and allies alike.

entries.name: Creating a Shaman
entries: To create a Shaman, consult the subsections which give you hit points, proficiencies, and starting equipment. Then look at the Shaman table to see which features you get at each level. The descriptions of those features appear below.

entries.name: Quick Build
entries: You can make a Shaman quickly with these suggestions: First, put your highest ability score in Wisdom, followed by Constitution or Dexterity; second, choose the Outlander background; third, choose the {@spell Produce Flame|XPHB} and {@spell Dancing Lights|XPHB} cantrips, along with the 1st-level {@spell Ice Knife|XGE} and {@spell Thunderwave|XPHB} spells.

entries.name: Multiclassing and the Shaman
entries: If your group uses the optional rule on multiclassing in the Player's Handbook, here's what you need to know if you choose Shaman as one of your classes.

entries.name: Ability Score Minimum
entries: As a multiclass character, you must have at least a Wisdom score of 13 to take a level in this class, or to take a level in another class if you are already a Shaman.

entries.name: Proficiencies Gained
entries: If Shaman isn't your initial class, here are the proficiencies you gain when you take your first level as a Shaman: light armor and simple weapons.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: To determine your available spell slots, you include all of your Shaman levels.

classFeature.name: Artful
entries: Your roguish talents extend beyond opportunistic attacks. For every sneak die in your pool (shown in the Skill Dice column of the Expert table), you can assign a die to one skill in which you are proficient. Whenever you make an ability check with that Skill, you can roll and add all assigned die to the result of that check.

Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can swap one dice to another skill. For example, a level 3 Expert proficient in Stealth and Acrobatics could gain a 2d6 bonus to Stealth, or a 1d6 bonus to Stealth and Acrobatics, or assign those dice to other skills.'

classFeature.name: Sneak Attack
entries: Your attacks are opportunistic, exploiting distraction or weakness in your opponents and their defenses. Once per turn, you can deal additional damage to a creature equal to your Sneak Dice (as shown in the Sneak Die column of the Expert table).

You can only deal this damage under two conditions: if you have Advantage on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or Ranged weapon; or if an ally who is not {@condition Incapacitated} is within 5 feet of the enemy, and you don't have Disadvantage on the roll.

classFeature.name: Thieves' Cant
entries: Your expertise comes with connections, and with those connections come various languages. You know {@language Thieves' Cant|PHB} and one other language of your choice.

classFeature.name: Cunning Action
entries: Your agility and talents allow you to move and act quickly. On your turn, you can take one of the {@action Dash|PHB}, {@action Disengage|PHB}, or {@action Hide|PHB} actions as a Bonus Action.

classFeature.name: Quick Thinking
entries: Your mind is sharp, allowing you to think on short notice and recover smoothly from failure.

items: You can make the {@action Influence|XPHB} , {@action Study|XPHB} or {@action Search|XPHB} actions as a bonus action on your turn.
If you do not succeed at an ability check that uses at least one sneak die, you can gain THP equal to twice your proficiency bonus.

classFeature.name: Reliable Talent
entries: Your talents are honed and your skills increased. Your Skill Die are now {@dice d8}s instead of {@dice d6}s.

classFeature.name: Optional Rule: Alternate Ability Hunter
entries: Hunters usually rely on their instincts, governed by Wisdom, their awareness of the world around them. But you may prefer that your Hunter gains an advantage through their wit and quick thinking, or their unbreakable resolve fueling their efforts.
If this is the case for your Hunter, you may prefer to use Intelligence or Charisma instead of Wisdom for your Hunter features. If you do so, make the following changes:

items: Features which specify your Wisdom modifier (such as Supreme Quarry) instead use the modifier of the chosen ability.
Your Hunter DC is calculated with that ability, instead of Wisdom.

classFeature.name: Instinct
entries: Hunters rely on their senses and instincts. You can apply yours more keenly than most creatures, granting you an edge in combat that you can exploit in various ways. Your Instinct recovers on a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

You also have a Hunter's Die, which determines the damage or bonus granted by some of your features. You have an amount of Instinct equal to your Hunter level plus two (as indicated in the Hunter Table) and additional equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 0).

classFeature.name: Quarry
entries: A Hunter needs a target. Once per turn, you can spend one {@classFeature Instinct|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight} and a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to designate a creature within 60 feet of you as your Quarry, the target of your hunt. The designation lasts for up to one hour, and when you hit that creature with an attack, you deal additional damage equal to your Hunter's Die of the same type as your weapon. You can have only one Quarry at a time.

classFeature.name: Fighting Style
entries: Your skills as a warrior are commendable, and you gain a {@filter Fighting Style Feat|feats|category=FS} of your choice.
Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace that Fighting Style feat with another.

classFeature.name: Survival Instincts
entries: A gut instinct guides your senses. Whenever you make an ability check using {@skill Perception|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}, you can spend one {@classFeature Instinct|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight} to add your Hunter's Die to the roll total.

activation.condition: When you make a Perception or Survival check

classFeature.name: Tricks
entries: A Hunter is flexible, able to adapt their skillset to most threats. These Tricks are combat techniques, unique skills or benefits to your skills, or modifications to your defenses. They may be informed by your Hunting Grounds.

At 2nd level, you know 2 {@filter Tricks|optionalfeatures|feature type=HTR}, and learn more as indicated in the Tricks column of the Hunter table. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can change one Trick for another that you qualify for, represented by your preparations for the day ahead.

If a Trick has prerequisites, you must meet them to gain that Trick. You can gain a Trick at the same time you meet its prerequisites. A level prerequisite refers to your level in this class. If you lose the prerequisite for a Trick, for example you change one Trick that another depends on, you may replace it with another Trick for which you meet the prerequisite.
Your Hunter features and Tricks share the same DC if they require a saving throw:

classFeature.name: Shrug It Off
entries: It takes a significant hit to phase you. Once per {@variantrule Short Rest}, you can spend one {@classFeature Instinct|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight} and a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to roll your Hunter's Die twice, add your Hunter level, and gain Temporary Hit Points equal to the total.

classFeature.name: Keen Eye
entries: When you make an attack roll against your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}, you can spend one {@classFeature Instinct|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight} to add your Hunter's Die to the roll.

activation.condition: When you make an attack roll against your Quarry

classFeature.name: Hunting Grounds
entries: When you reach 3rd level, you distinguish yourself from other Hunters by calling on the skills developed in your Hunting Grounds, the place you honed your skills. Your Hunting Grounds grant you features at 3rd level, and again at 7th, 11th, and 15th level.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Hunter levels 8, 12, and 16.

classFeature.name: Measured Quarry
entries: Choose a hunting discipline. When you designate your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}, you gain the associated benefit.

classFeature.name: Relentless Approach
entries: Your Quarry cannot {@condition Frighten} you.

classFeature.name: Watchful Approach
entries: Your Quarry cannot {@condition Charm} you.

classFeature.name: Tactical Approach
entries: You learn your Quarry's resistances, vulnerabilities or immunities to any damage or conditions.

classFeature.name: Offensive Hunter
entries: At 6th level, your skill as a Hunter have grown and you develop new techniques to fell larger foes or to cleave through their minions. Choose one of the following:

classFeature.name: Focused Assault
entries: You deal an additional {@dice 1d4} damage when you damage a creature that is below its maximum hit points.

classFeature.name: Considered Strikes
entries: You score a critical hit on attacks when rolling a 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20}. Whenever you roll a critical hit, you deal additional damage equal to one roll of your Hunter's Die.

classFeature.name: Thin the Herd
entries: Once on each of your turns when you attack a creature, you can immediately make another attack against a different creature within 10 feet of the target that is within your reach or range.

classFeature.name: Sixth Sense
entries: You can mark your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight} without being able to see them and within a range of 600 feet. You have advantage on any Wisdom or Intelligence checks made to find your Quarry or see through its illusions, and your quarry lasts up to eight hours.

classFeature.name: Hunting Grounds Feature
entries: When you reach 7th level, you gain another feature from your Hunting Grounds.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Hunter levels 12 and 16.

classFeature.name: Pressured Quarry
entries: Choose a hunting discipline. When you designate your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}, you gain that benefit.

classFeature.name: Relentless Pressure
entries: When you hit your Quarry with an attack, all other attacks you make against your Quarry before the start of your have a +3 bonus to hit until the start of your next turn.

classFeature.name: Watchful Guard
entries: When your Quarry deals damage to you with a feature that targets only you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to halve the damage you take from that feature.

activation.condition: When your Quarry deals damage to you with a feature that targets only you

description.chatFlavor: Your careful watch lets you protect yourself from danger. Take half damage from the triggering effect.

classFeature.name: Tactical Disruption
entries: After your Quarry makes an attack roll, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to impose a penalty to the roll equal to your Hunter's Die. At the additional cost of one {@classFeature Instinct|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}, you can do this when your Quarry makes a saving throw.

activation.condition: When your Quarry makes an attack roll
When your Quarry makes a saving throw

classFeature.name: Quick Thinking
entries: When you fail a saving throw, you can spend one {@classFeature Instinct|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight} to add your Hunter's Die to the roll, potentially turning it into a success.

activation.condition: When you fail a saving throw

classFeature.name: Defensive Hunter
entries: At 10th level, your skill as a Hunter have grown further and you develop new techniques to help you evade danger. Choose one of the following:

classFeature.name: Quickstep
entries: Opportunity attacks against you are made at {@variantrule Disadvantage}.

classFeature.name: Pattern Recognition
entries: After a creature hits you with an attack, you gain a +3 bonus to your {@variantrule Armour Class|XPHB|AC} against all other attacks made by that creature until the end of its turn.

classFeature.name: Evasion
entries: When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

classFeature.name: Hunting Grounds Feature
entries: When you reach 11th level, you gain another feature from your Hunting Grounds.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Hunter level 16.

classFeature.name: Cornered Quarry
entries: Choose a hunting discipline. When you designate your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}, you gain that benefit.

classFeature.name: Relentless Strikes
entries: Your attacks against your Quarry deal additional damage equal to your Wisdom modifier.

classFeature.name: Watchful Poise
entries: You have an additional 5 feet of reach when attempting to attack your Quarry with a melee weapon. If you use a ranged weapon, you do not suffer disadvantage on attacks outside of the weapon's normal range that are made against your Quarry.

classFeature.name: Tactical Isolation
entries: When you attack your Quarry, you can instead end the Quarry and make an attack against every other creature of your choice within your reach (if you use a melee weapon), or within 10 feet of your quarry (if you use a ranged weapon).

classFeature.name: Refined Instincts
entries: You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws, and one of your choice of Charisma or Intelligence saving throws.

classFeature.name: Hunting Grounds Feature
entries: When you reach 15th level, you gain another feature from your Hunting Grounds.

classFeature.name: Supernatural Hunter
entries: Your skills as a Hunter grow again, to the extent that your abilities seem almost supernatural. Choose one of the following abilities, which you can use once per {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}:

classFeature.name: Vanish
entries: You can spend a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to become {@condition Invisible|XPHB} until the end of your next turn. While invisible, you can pass through objects and creatures, and cannot be {@condition Grappled} or {@condition Restrained}. If you end your turn within an object or creature's space, you take {@dice 3d10} force damage and are shunted to the nearest available space.

classFeature.name: Blur
entries: You double your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} this turn (no action required). If you take damage before the start of your next turn, any movement you didn't use on your turn can instead be used to reduce that damage, spending 1 feet of unused movement for every 1 point of damage.

classFeature.name: Reaper
entries: Attacks made as part of the {@action Attack} action this turn deal additional damage equal to your Hunter's Die. If you reduce a creature to zero hit points with these attacks, you can take another {@variantrule Action} this turn.

classFeature.name: Doomed Quarry
entries: Choose a hunting discipline. When you designate your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}, you gain that benefit.

classFeature.name: Relentless Assault
entries: You have advantage on attacks against your Quarry.

classFeature.name: Watchful Resolve
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage} on any saving throws you make against your Quarry and its effects.

classFeature.name: Tactical Dominance
entries: You force your Quarry's attention, protecting your allies. The first time each turn your Quarry targets one of your allies, your Quarry has {@variantrule Disadvantage} on its attack (if it attacks), or that ally has resistance to any damage dealt and advantage on any saving throws they are forced to make by your Quarry.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon Feat|feats|category=EB} or another {@filter feat|feats|} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Hunter's Zenith
entries: Your Wisdom score increases by 2, and so does your Strength or Dexterity score (you choose), both up to a maximum of 30.

You can have up to two creatures as your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight} at any one time, and when you mark one you can mark another at no cost. Choosing another Quarry only ends your previous Quarry if you would have more than two, in which case you choose which to end.
At this level, you also gain access to a unique and powerful Trick: Relentless, Watchful, or Tactical Hunter.

classFeature.name: Optional Rule: Alternate Ability Shaman
entries: While Shamans channel nature's magic in a similar mystical manner to druids, it is also possible to learn this power through study, or through force of will in dedication to nature.
If this is the case for your Shaman, you may prefer to use Intelligence or Charisma instead of Wisdom for your shaman features. If you do so, make the following changes:

items: Wherever you would use Wisdom for your shaman features or specialism features, such as your Spellcasting or Rune features, you instead use your chosen ability.
If you choose Intelligence, you replace Charisma as a saving throw proficiency given by this class with Intelligence.
A multiclassed character would require a 13 in the chosen ability (instead of Wisdom) to take a level in this class, or take a level in another if Shaman is your first class.

classFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: Your experience in nature has infused you with the primordial magics of the world. This could be a life in a tribe, time spent wandering the wilds and finding a spirit, or unexpected communion with a nature deity. Whatever its origin, it fuels your spellcasting. You can channel these primal magics to strike those who would defy nature, restore your allies, and manipulate the world around you.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: At 1st level, you know two cantrips of your choice from the {@filter Shaman spell list|spells|class=Shaman (Starlight)}. Whenever you gain a Shaman level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another from the Shaman spell list. You learn an additional cantrip of your choice at 7th level as shown in the Cantrips column of the Shaman Features table.
Whenever you gain a Shaman level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another from the {@filter Shaman spell list|spells|class=Shaman (Starlight)}.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Shaman table above shows how many spell slots you have to cast your {@filter Shaman spells|spells|class=Shaman (Starlight)} of 1st-level or higher. To cast one, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all of your expended spell slots when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest}.

entries.name: Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher
entries: You know two 1st-level spells of your choice from the {@filter Shaman spell list|spells|class=Shaman (Starlight)}.
You learn an additional Shaman spell of your choice every level, and every other level from level 11 onwards.

Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the Shaman spells you know and replace it with another spell from the {@filter Shaman spell list|spells|class=Shaman (Starlight)}, which must also be a level for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for Shaman spells as you draw magic from your connection to nature. You use your Wisdom when a Shaman spell refers to your spellcasting ability, and you use your Wisdom modifier whenever you set the saving throw DC or make a spell attack roll for one of your Shaman spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use a {@item druidic focus|XPHB} as a spellcasting focus for your shaman spells. You or your DM may decide it more appropriate to use an {@item arcane focus|XPHB}, depending on how your shaman learned their magic.

entries.name: Ritual Casting
entries: Your connection to nature can be channeled with time, at less cost to yourself. You can cast a shaman spell you know as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag.

classFeature.name: Paths of the Shaman
entries: You dedicate yourself to one of the following shamanic paths: {@optfeature Path of the Conduit|Starlight}, {@optfeature Path of the Runeblade|Starlight}, {@optfeature Path of the Conjurer|Starlight}, or the {@optfeature Path of the Seer|Starlight}.

classFeature.name: Primordial Runes
entries: Your access to the primal forces of the world has granted you access to Primordial Runes, fragments of primal spirits which can enhance your own power, grant you new abilities or empower your existing ones.

At 2nd level, you gain 2 Primordial Runes of your choice. A list of the available options can be found on the {@filter Optional Features|optionalfeatures|feature type=PRU} page. When you gain certain Shaman levels, you gain additional runes of your choice, as shown in the Runes column of the Shaman table.
Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the runes you know and replace it with another that you could learn at that level.

If a rune has prerequisites, you must meet them to gain that rune. You can gain a rune at the same time you meet its prerequisites. A level prerequisite refers to your level in this class. If you lose the prerequisite for a rune, by changing your elemental affinity for example, you may replace it with another rune for which you meet the prerequisite.

classFeature.name: Elemental Affinity
entries: You are attuned with all aspects of nature, but one speaks to you much more strongly: {@optfeature Affinity with Flame|Starlight}, {@optfeature Affinity with Frost|Starlight}, {@optfeature Affinity with Lightning|Starlight}, {@optfeature Affinity with Thunder|Starlight}, or {@optfeature Affinity with Acid|Starlight}
When you choose an Elemental Affinity, you gain a cantrip that deals that damage type and you become resistant to that damage type.
You will also gain access to a series of Primordial Runes that can deepen your affinity.

classFeature.name: Elemental Origin
entries: At 3rd level, you determine the origin of your shaman abilities. This could be the source that they are drawn from, where your Shaman grew up or learned their magic, or the specific location they first unlocked their magical gifts.
This origin grants you features at 3rd level, and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

classFeature.name: Elemental Origin Feature
entries: At 6th level, you gain a feature granted by your elemental origin.

classFeature.name: Down the Path
entries: You gain an additional benefit from your Path of the Shaman.

entries.name: Path of the Conduit
entries: You learn an additional Shaman cantrip of your choice and gain a bonus to Arcana checks equal to your spellcasting modifier.

entries.name: Path of the Runeblade
entries: Your Runeblade deals an additional {@dice 1d4} damage of a type matching your Elemental Affinity.

entries.name: Path of the Conjurer
entries: You know up to four totems from the list, and the list gains these additional options:

items: {@b {@creature Unerring Aim Nature Spirit Totem|Starlight|Unerring Aim}.} Creatures in this emanation can reroll an attack they miss once each round.

{@b {@creature Vortex Nature Spirit Totem|Starlight|Vortex}.} Creatures of your choice within range of this totem take damage of the type associated with your elemental affinity whenever they start their turn or enter the Totem's Emanation. The damage is a number of {@dice d4}s equal to your proficiency bonus.

{@b {@creature Life Nature Spirit Totem|Starlight|Life}.} Creatures within this totem's emanation have resistance to necrotic damage, and regain one hit point at the start of their turn if they do not have any.
{@b {@creature Enforcement Nature Spirit Totem|Starlight|Enforcement}.} Creatures within this totem's emanation gain temporary hit points and cannot be moved against their will.

entries.name: Path of the Seer
entries: You have advantage on Initiative rolls, and can swap your Initiative and a willing ally's at the start of combat.

classFeature.name: Elemental Origin Feature
entries: At 10th level, you gain a feature granted by your elemental origin.

classFeature.name: Elemental Origin Feature
entries: At 14th level, you gain a feature granted by your elemental origin.

classFeature.name: Elemental Embodiment
entries: At 18th level, you are a paragon of your chosen element. You become immune to the damage type of your chosen elemental affinity.

classFeature.name: Spiritual Avatar
entries: At 20th level, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action} to channel the spirits of nature directly for one minute, using yourself as a conduit. This might change your appearance as you choose to suit your elemental affinity or origin, such as your head being lit with flames, or your skin being covered with frost.
While this state is active, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a flying speed of 50 feet.
Whenever you cast a Shaman spell that has a casting time of one {@variantrule Action}, you can cast it using a {@variantrule Bonus Action} instead.

entries: At this level, you also have access to a Primordial Rune specific to your subclass that can enhance your Spiritual Avatar in another way.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest}.

classFeature.name: Fighting Style
entries: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. You can't take the same Fighting Style option more than once, even if you get to choose again.

classFeature.name: Favored Enemy and Natural Explorer improvements
Metamagic
entries: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to twist your spells to suit your needs. You gain two Metamagic options of your choice. You gain another one at 10th and 17th level.
You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it, unless otherwise noted.

classFeature.name: Eldritch Invocations
entries: In your study of occult lore, you have unearthed eldritch invocations, fragments of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability.

At 2nd level, you gain two eldritch invocations of your choice. Your invocation options are detailed at the end of the class description. When you gain certain warlock levels, you gain additional invocations of your choice, as shown in the Invocations Known column of the Warlock table.
Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the invocations you know and replace it with another invocation that you could learn at that level.

If an eldritch invocation has prerequisites, you must meet them to learn it. You can learn the invocation at the same time that you meet its prerequisites. A level prerequisite refers to your level in this class.

effects.name: Hamstrung
effects.description: Hit by a hamstring blow, this character's Speed has been reduced by 15 feet until the start of the attacker's next turn.

effects.name: Staggered
effects.description: Hit by a staggering blow, this character has Disadvantage on the next Saving Throw it makes, and it can't make Opportunity Attacks until the start of the attacker's next turn.

effects.name: Sundered

effects.name: Inspired
effects.description: You have received Bardic Inspiration. Once within the next hour when you fail a D20 Test, you can roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to the d20, potentially turning the failure into a success. A Bardic Inspiration die is expended when it's rolled.

effects.name: Turned
effects.description: For that duration, it tries to move as far from you as it can on its turns. This effect ends early on the creature if it takes any damage, if you have the Incapacitated condition, or if you die.

descriptionEntries.name: Martial Arts Die
entries: You can roll [[lookup @scale.monk.die]] in place of the normal damage of your Unarmed Strike or Monk weapons. This die changes as you gain Monk levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of the Monk Features table.

descriptionEntries.name: Dexterous Attacks
entries: You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes and Monk weapons. In addition, when you use the Grapple or Shove option of your Unarmed Strike, you can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier to determine the save DC.

effects.name: Disengaged
effects.description: Your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks for the rest of the current turn.

activation.condition: When you roll initiative
When an attack roll hits you and its damage includes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage
If you reduce the damage to 0

range.special: 5 feet for melee attacks or 60 feet for ranged attacks

activation.condition: Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Monk weapon or an Unarmed Strike

effects.name: Slowed
effects.description: The target's Speed is halved until the start of your next turn, and the next attack roll made against the target before then has Advantage

activation.condition: When you expend a Focus Point to use Patient Defense
When an attack roll hits you and its damage includes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage
If you reduce the damage to 0

range.special: 5 feet for melee attacks or 60 feet for ranged attacks

activation.condition: At the start of your turn

classFeature.name: Fighting Style
entries: You gain a {@filter Fighting Style feat|feats|category=FS} of your choice. Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose the {@feat Blessed Warrior|XPHB} Fighting Style.

effects.description: You know the location of any creature of those types within 60 feet of yourself, and you know its creature type. Within the same radius, you also detect the presence of any place or object that has been consecrated or desecrated, as with the Hallow spell.

effects.name: Courageous
effects.description: You and your allies have Immunity to the Frightened condition while in your Aura of Protection.

classFeature.name: Fighting Style
entries: You gain a {@filter Fighting Style feat|feats|category=FS} of your choice. Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose the {@feat Druidic Warrior|XPHB} Fighting Style.

activation.condition: Whenever you finish a Short Rest
When you deal Sneak Attack damage
When you deal Sneak Attack damage

effects.name: Cunning Strike: Poisoned
effects.description: On a failed save, the target has the Poisoned condition for 1 minute.

activation.condition: When you deal Snack Attack damage
When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack roll
When you deal Sneak Attack damage
When you deal Sneak Attack damage

effects.name: Devious Strikes: Dazed
effects.description: On its next turn, the target can do only one of the following: move or take an action or a Bonus Action.

activation.condition: When you deal Sneak Attack damage

effects.name: Devious Strikes: Knocked Out
effects.description: The target has the Unconscious condition for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. The Unconscious target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

activation.condition: When you deal Sneak Attack damage

effects.name: Devious Strikes: Blinded
effects.description: The target has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn

activation.condition: When you fail a D20 Test

effects.description: The spell save DC of your Sorcerer spells increases by 1. You have Advantage on the attack rolls of Sorcerer spells you cast.

classFeature.name: Sorcery Points
entries: You have 2 Sorcery Points, and you gain more as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Sorcery Points column of the Sorcerer Features table. You can't have more Sorcery Points than the number shown in the table for your level. You regain all expended Sorcery Points when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

activation.condition: When you use Magical Cunning

effects.name: Signature
effects.description: Choose two level 3 spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, and you can cast each of them once at level 3 without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can't cast them in this way again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Edge of the World
entries: Borderland Hunters walk on the borders of the Material Plane and its mirror, the Feywilds, stalking the creatures that live there. Living in shades of grey and dim light, they have mastered the borders and can briefly change where they reside, striking terror no matter where a creature escapes to.

subclassFeature.name: Skills from the Borderland
entries: {@i 3rd-level Borderland Hunter feature}
Your experience in dealing with creatures of the between-realm has given you skills related to reading intention and concealing your own.
You gain proficiency with two of the following skills: {@skill Insight|XPHB}, {@skill Deception|XPHB}, {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}, or {@skill Arcana|XPHB}.
Additionally, you gain proficiency with {@item Navigator's tools|XPHB} and {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB}, so you are never lost, and can identify the dangerous flora of the feywilds.

subclassFeature.name: Border-world Quarries
entries: {@i 3rd-level Borderland Hunter feature}
Ghosts and Fae... tricksy, aye. Lucky for you, there's a fancy fire that should still get 'em sweating!
When you damage your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}, you can choose for the additional damage dealt by your Hunter's Die to be Radiant damage.

subclassFeature.name: Ethereal Shift
entries: {@i 3rd-level Borderland Hunter feature}

You can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to shift into a state between the planes. While in this state, which lasts for one minute, you can move through other creatures freely. If you move through a creature this way, they take necrotic damage equal to a roll of your Hunter's Die. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.
If you end your turn in another creature's space, you are shunted harmlessly to the nearest available space. Ethereal Shift ends if you become {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} or die.
You can use this feature for free once per {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, otherwise it costs two {@classFeature Instinct|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}.

activation.condition: When you pass through a creature's space while using Ethereal Shift

subclassFeature.name: Expert
entries: {@i 7th-level Borderland Hunter feature}

The skills you gained from the Borderlands have improved. You gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in the skills you chose, and one of the tools from, your {@subclassFeature Skills from the Borderland|Hunter|Starlight|Borderland|Starlight|3|Starlight|Skills from the Borderland} feature.

subclassFeature.name: Ethereal Shift Improvement
entries: {@i 7th-level Borderland Hunter feature}
While using Ethereal Shift, you can cast {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} once on each of your turns (no spell slot required).

subclassFeature.name: Fae Tricks
entries: {@i 11th-level Borderland Hunter feature}

When a creature hits you with an attack, spell, or other effect while you are using Ethereal Shift, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to end Ethereal Shift and teleport up to 30 feet away, potentially causing the effect to miss.
Regardless of if you evade the effect, the attacking creature must make a Wisdom saving throw or take {@dice 4d8} psychic damage. This damage increases to {@dice 5d10} at level 15.

activation.condition: When a creature affects you while you are using Ethereal Shift

subclassFeature.name: Grave Step
entries: {@i 15th-level Borderland Hunter feature}
While using Ethereal Shift, you have {@sense Truesight|XPHB} out to a range of 30 feet.

Additionally, the necrotic damage you deal by passing through a creature's space increases to two rolls of your Hunter's Die. When you cast Misty Step using Ethereal Shift, you can deal this damage to all creatures in a 5-foot line between the space you teleport from and your destination.

subclassFeature.name: Planeswalker
entries: Extraplanar Hunters walk the outer planes, dealing with Celestials, Demons and Aberrations alike. Time spent in these outer regions inevitably grants a taste of the power these creatures wield, which Extraplanar Hunters manipulate to their own end. They may protect other planes from these creatures, go on missions in these areas, or simply live their lives there.

subclassFeature.name: Skills from the Outer Planes
entries: {@i 3rd-level Extraplanar Hunter feature}
Your experience in the outer planes has taught you much about magic and the beliefs and mythologies of others.
You gain proficiency with 2 of the following skills: {@skill Arcana|XPHB}, {@skill Religion|XPHB}, {@skill Insight}, or {@skill Persuasion}.

Additionally, you gain proficiency with any {@item Gaming Set|XPHB} and {@item Cook's Utensils}, as some creatures from these planes are known to enjoy games, and their food may not be to your liking.

subclassFeature.name: Outer-planes Quarries
entries: {@i 3rd-level Extraplanar Hunter feature}
You gotta deal with a wide range of creatures in the outer planes, nothing works against all of them. So try to hit it where it hurts: right between the eyes.
When you damage your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}, you can choose for the additional damage dealt by your Hunter's Die to be Psychic damage.

subclassFeature.name: Planar Gift
entries: {@i 3rd-level Extraplanar Hunter feature}

Your exposure to otherworldly magics has given you access to a pool of energy you can derive power from. It can hold a number of your Hunter's Die equal to your Proficiency Bonus and refills when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. When you damage your Quarry, you can add one Hunter's Die to the pool.

subclassFeature.name: Aberrant Ward
entries: {@i 3rd-level Extraplanar Hunter feature}

Pulling from the Psionic Powers of Aberrations, you can protect your allies. When another creature within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to roll any number of dice from your Planar Gift, reducing the damage they take by the total rolled.

activation.condition: When a nearby ally takes damage

subclassFeature.name: Expert
entries: {@i 7th-level Extraplanar Hunter feature}

The skills you gained from the outer planes have improved. You gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in the skills you chose, and one of the tools from, your {@subclassFeature Skills from the Outer Planes|Hunter|Starlight|Extraplanar|Starlight|3|Starlight|Skills from the Outer Planes feature}.

subclassFeature.name: Celestial Dusting
entries: {@i 7th-level Extraplanar Hunter feature}
When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can spend and roll one die from your Planar Gift to grant that many temporary hit points to yourself or a creature within 10 feet of you.
If you damage your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}, you can instead use the Hunter's Die rolled as part of the attack.

activation.condition: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack

subclassFeature.name: Infernal Edge
entries: {@i 11th-level Extraplanar Hunter feature}

Once on each of your turns, you can use a die from your Planar Gift to attempt to poison a creature when you hit them with a weapon attack. The target takes additional necrotic damage equal to a roll of your Hunter's Die, and must make a Constitution saving throw or become {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} until the end of your next turn.

activation.condition: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack

subclassFeature.name: Planar Boon
entries: {@i 15th-level Extraplanar Hunter feature}
Your gifts from the outer planes have grown in power:

items: Aberrant Ward now pushes the attacking creature 10 feet away from the ally you protect with it.
Celestial Dusting can also be used to restore hit points to a creature, and its range is 30 feet.
The target of your Infernal Edge has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the saving throw if your target is a Fiend, Celestial or Aberration.

subclassFeature.name: Bounty Hunter
entries: Those who hunt in this environment have a unique challenge. Finding one creature in a crowd, instead of a forest. Vertical, cramped terrain, with winding alleys and hidden paths. And a thousand places to disappear in plain sight. Urban Hunters cut through this noise, finding their marks and stopping them from getting away - if they ever saw you in the first place.

subclassFeature.name: Skills from the City
entries: {@i 3rd-level Urban Hunter feature}
Your experience navigating the cities has taught you how to find secrets, and how to get your way.
You gain proficiency with two of the following three skills: {@skill Investigation|XPHB}, {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}, and {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}.
Additionally, you gain proficiency with {@item Forgery Kit|XPHB|Forgery Kits} and {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, to help you gain access to well-guarded places.

subclassFeature.name: Everyman Quarries
entries: {@i 3rd-level Urban Hunter feature}
Poison isn't what it used to be, and if you're a good soul you'll be hunting assassins yourself. It's a rare citygoer who can resist something like this, though.
When you damage your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}, you can choose for the additional damage dealt by your Hunter's Die to be Necrotic damage.

subclassFeature.name: Cripple Foe
entries: {@i 3rd-level Urban Hunter feature}
The best way to chase a creature is to prevent them getting away in the first place.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can spend one {@classFeature Instinct|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight} to make a special attack against a target within your reach or range; they must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they are {@condition Slowed|Starlight} and take damage equal to a roll of your Hunter's Die plus your Wisdom modifier. On a successful save, they are {@condition Hampered|Starlight} and take half damage instead.

subclassFeature.name: Expert
entries: {@i 7th-level Urban Hunter feature}

Your city-life skills have improved. You gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in the skills you chose, and one of the tools from, your {@subclassFeature Skills from the City|Hunter|Starlight|Urban|Starlight|3|Starlight|Skills from the City} feature.

subclassFeature.name: Seeker
entries: {@i 7th-level Urban Hunter feature}

You have a knack for finding people. You can spend one {@classFeature Instinct|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight} and an {@variantrule Action} to sense the direction to a creature as per the {@spell Locate Creature|XPHB} spell. This lasts for ten minutes and does not require your {@status concentration|concentrating}.

subclassFeature.name: Silent Killer
entries: {@i 11th-level Urban Hunter feature}
You can take the {@action Hide|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

While unseen by a creature, you can replace one attack from your {@action Attack} action with a stealth strike. On hit, the target must make an Intelligence saving throw or be {@condition Silenced|Starlight} and {@condition Deafened|XPHB} until the start of your next turn, they take additional damage equal to your Hunter's Die, and your position is not revealed to that creature. You can do this only once on each of your turns.

subclassFeature.name: Opportunist
entries: {@i 15th-level Urban Hunter feature}

When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points, you can immediately move up to half your speed without provoking {@variantrule Opportunity Attacks}. As part of this movement, you can take the {@action Hide} action, and if you end the movement hidden then you become {@condition Invisible} until the end of your next turn.
The invisibility ends if you make an attack or force a creature to make a saving throw.

subclassFeature.name: Beast Hunter
entries: Horizon Hunters strive to be the best, hunting anything from sky to sea. They weaken their quarries in speed in strength, claim trophies from their strikes and even have the expertise to handle packs of creatures. They might do it for fame and fortune, they might do it to protect the innocent from the dangers of the wild, or they might simply hunt for the thrill of bettering themselves.

subclassFeature.name: Skills from the Wilds
entries: {@i 3rd-level Horizon Hunter feature}
In order to hunt beasts, you must travel far and learn how to cope with animals of all temperaments and sizes.
You gain proficiency with two of the following three skills: {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB}, {@skill Athletics|XPHB}, and {@skill Survival|XPHB}.
Additionally, you gain proficiency with piloting air or water vehicles, and with a {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Bestial Quarries
entries: {@i 3rd-level Horizon Hunter feature}
If you must slay beasts, I don't know a beast alive that's a fan of fire. Hopefully by the time you find one that {@i doesn't} mind fire, you can work your way around that.
When you damage your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}, you can choose for the additional damage dealt by your Hunter's Die to be Fire damage.

subclassFeature.name: Declaw
entries: {@i 3rd-level Horizon Hunter feature}

You can attempt to cripple your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}. Once per turn when you make a successful attack with the {@variantrule Attack|XPHB|Attack action} against your Quarry, you can spend one {@classFeature Instinct|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight} to force it to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you can disable one of its attack options (the DM chooses which) until the start of your next turn. If you forgo dealing damage, it has disadvantage on the saving throw.

subclassFeature.name: Trophies
entries: {@i 3rd-level Horizon Hunter feature}

When you roll a 20 on an attack roll against your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}, it drops a trophy, an item of significance such as a serpent's venomous fang. You can sell a Trophy in your downtime for 10gp times the creature's CR. At your DM's discretion, you may require a Wisdom (Survival) check and {@dice 1d4} days to find a suitable buyer - in these cases, the item may sell for more.

subclassFeature.name: Expert
entries: {@i 7th-level Horizon Hunter feature}

Your skills from the wild have improved. You gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in the skills you chose, and one of the tools from, your {@subclassFeature Skills from the Wilds|Hunter|Starlight|Horizon|Starlight|3|Starlight|Skills from the Wilds} feature.

subclassFeature.name: Roaming
entries: {@i 7th-level Horizon Hunter feature}
Your walking speed increases by 10 feet, and you gain a Climb and Swim speed equal to your walking speed.
You can hold your breath underwater for an additional number of minutes equal to your Wisdom modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Pack Hunting
entries: {@i 7th-level Horizon Hunter feature}
When your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight} dies, you can designate another creature of the same type as your Quarry immediately (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Siphon Speed
entries: {@i 11th-level Horizon Hunter feature}

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack, you can deal extra damage equal to your Hunter's Die and force it to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed saving throw, the creature is {@condition Slowed|Starlight} until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Apex Hunter
entries: {@i 15th-level Horizon Hunter feature}
When a creature fails their saving throw against Siphon Speed, your movement speeds are replaced with theirs until the start of your next turn, unless yours are higher.
When you hit your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}, its immunities are treated as resistance, and you bypass its resistances.

subclassFeature.name: Storyteller
entries: Fable Hunters gained their knowledge from study, and almost all of them have a common goal: to be a Hunter that would be discussed in the very books and tales they learned from. A Fable Hunter aims to live forever, immortalised in stories told around a fireplace and studies of combat strategy. A Fable Hunter wants to take on creatures of Legendary power; and a Fable Hunter wants to win. To this end, they learn their foe, and direct their allies to victory. Success comes before personal glory.

{@note A 'Legendary Creature' is one that has Legendary (or similar, such as Mythic) actions. Typically, having only a Lair Action would not qualify a creature. Work with your DM to define what a legendary creature means in your campaign.}

subclassFeature.name: Skills of Yore
entries: {@i 3rd-level Fable Hunter feature}
For your tale to be told, you must develop the quick wits and knowledge to tell it.
You gain proficiency with two of the following skills: {@skill Perception|XPHB}, {@skill Nature|XPHB}, and {@skill Performance|XPHB}.
Additionally, you gain proficiency with {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} and {@item Woodcarver's Tools}, to keep your group well-supplied.

subclassFeature.name: Epic Quarries
entries: {@i 3rd-level Fable Hunter feature}
The toughest creatures earned their rep', and they come in all shapes and sizes. Getting past defenses like that is tricky for even the strongest mages... but you might have a way.
When you damage your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}, you can choose for the additional damage dealt by your Hunter's Die to be Force damage.

subclassFeature.name: Commander
entries: {@i 3rd-level Fable Hunter feature}

Whenever you make an attack with the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can instead spend one {@classFeature Instinct|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight} to command an ally. The ally you choose can use their {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move up to their {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, or make an attack against your Quarry. The attack has a bonus to the damage roll equal to a roll of your Hunter's Die.

activation.condition: When you make an attack and command an ally to attack instead

subclassFeature.name: Expert
entries: {@i 7th-level Fable Hunter feature}

Your story-making skills have grown. You gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in the skills you chose, and one of the tools from, from your {@subclassFeature Skills of Yore|Hunter|Starlight|Fable|Starlight|3|Starlight|} feature.

subclassFeature.name: Rally
entries: {@i 7th-level Fable Hunter feature}

Whenever you make an attack with the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can instead spend one {@classFeature Instinct|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight} to inspire a friendly creature within 60 feet of you. That creature gains temporary hit points equal to a roll of your Hunter's Die plus your Wisdom modifier, and their next successful attack deals additional damage equal to your Hunter's Die.

activation.condition: When you take the Attack action and choose to inspire an ally instead

description.chatFlavor: An ally within 60 feet gains temporary hit points and their next successful attack deals additional damage equal to your Hunter's Die.

subclassFeature.name: Hunter's Call
entries: {@i 11th-level Fable Hunter feature}

Once per {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and one {@classFeature Instinct|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight} to mark one target with a special Quarry until the start of your next turn. Whenever any creature deals damage to the target, they deal additional damage equal to your Hunter's Die.

subclassFeature.name: Commanding Shout
entries: {@i 15th-level Fable Hunter feature}

Once per {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to imbue allies within 30 feet of you with epic tenacity. Until the end of your next turn, affected creatures cannot be reduced below one hit point or killed, their {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} cannot be reduced, and they cannot be {@condition Stunned|XPHB} or {@condition Restrained|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Legendary Resilience
entries: {@i 15th-level Fable Hunter feature}

When you are targeted by a Legendary Action (and similar actions such as Mythic Actions), you can either gain advantage on a saving throw you are forced to make against it or gain resistance to any damage dealt by it.

subclassFeature.name: Off-worlder
entries: Primordial Hunters have stalked the realms of the elements, managing these supernatural powers and places for their own end. A Primordial Hunter may roam these places to conquer them, or to channel their powers to enhance their prowess in other ways. They may have learned these skills through direct exposure, an elemental teacher such as a Djinn, or through rigourous study as if it were magic.

subclassFeature.name: Skills from the Arcane
entries: {@i 3rd-level Primordial Hunter feature}
These powers are mysterious, necessitating study and a good understanding of the world in which you live.
You gain proficiency with two of the following skills: {@skill Arcana|XPHB}, {@skill Nature|XPHB}, and {@skill History|XPHB}.
Additionally, you gain proficiency with {@item Mason's Tools|XPHB} and {@item Alchemist's Supplies}, to shape your world and use its ingredients.

subclassFeature.name: Preferred Plane
entries: {@i 3rd-level Primordial Hunter feature}
Thanks to your experience, teacher, study, or just a grudge, you are more familiar with one plane than the others, and it acts as a focus for your talents.
Choose one of the following:

items: {@b Plane of Earth.} The damage type is Bludgeoning.
{@b Plane of Water.} The damage type is Cold.
{@b Plane of Fire.} The damage type is Fire.
{@b Plane of Air.} The damage type is Lightning.

entries: {@b Abjure Energy.} You have resistance to the chosen damage type.

subclassFeature.name: Ancient Quarries
entries: {@i 3rd-level Primordial Hunter feature}
What has your study taught you? These creatures are often too intelligent for their own good, or dumb without being mindless, with little inbetween. That means you aim for the head.
When you damage your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight}, you can choose for the additional damage dealt by your Hunter's Die to be Psychic damage.
Alternatively, the damage type can be the one chosen in your {@subclassFeature Preferred Plane|Hunter|Starlight|Primordial|Starlight|3|Starlight}.

subclassFeature.name: Evoke Elements
entries: {@i 3rd-level Primordial Hunter feature}

Once per turn when you make an attack as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can instead spend two {@classFeature Instinct|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight} to replace it with an evocation of energy from the point you targeted with the attack. Each creature other than you within 10 feet of the chosen point must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking two rolls of your Hunter's Die as damage (of a type matching your {@subclassFeature Preferred Plane|Hunter|Starlight|Primordial|Starlight|3|Starlight}) and half as much on a success. Your Quarry has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the saving throw.

activation.condition: When you make an attack and replace it

subclassFeature.name: Expert
entries: {@i 7th-level Primordial Hunter feature}

Your skills of elemental exploration have grown. You gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in the skills you chose, and one of the tools from, from your {@subclassFeature Skills from the Arcane|Hunter|Starlight|Primordial|Starlight|3|Starlight|} feature.

subclassFeature.name: Conjure Elemental
entries: {@i 7th-level Primordial Hunter feature}

You can perform a 1-hour ritual to channel the primordial energy that infuses all things into an elemental spirit that accompanies you. If the spirit enters an area of {@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB|antimagic} or is targeted with {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB}, it vanishes and must be resummoned. It does not act as its own entity in combat but can assist you in other ways while it is present. The spirit's form depends on your {@subclassFeature Preferred Plane|Hunter|Starlight|Primordial|Starlight|3|Starlight}.

items: {@b Dustling (Earth).} Appearing as a collection of small rocks or soot and dust, the Dustling can help you move objects or creatures. You add your Hunter's Die to ability checks made to move objects, your carrying capacity increases by 50lbs, and once per turn when you deal Bludgeoning damage to a creature you can move it 5 feet horizontally.

{@b Tidesling (Water).} As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, the Tidesling cools a surface: a dangerously hot surface becomes safe, and a cool surface becomes frozen, in a 10-foot square within 5 feet of you; a creature that walks on this surface must make a Dexterity saving throw or fall {@condition Prone|XPHB}, and the surface lasts for one minute. Once per turn, it can snuff out any fire in a 5-foot square within 30 feet of you. Finally, the Tidesling cushions your landings: if you would take damage from falling, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce it by three times your Hunter level and not be {@condition Prone|XPHB}.

{@b Cinderling (Fire).} The Cinderling emits {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} up to a maximum of 20 feet, and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for a further 20 feet. You change the range and colour of the light as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB|XPHB}. Once per turn, the Cinderling can also start a fire on a flammable object (no action required). Once per turn when you deal Fire damage to a creature, you can end the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition on it and cause it to glow. This lasts for one minute or until the creature spends an {@variantrule Action|XPHB} to end the effect.

{@b Cloudling (Air).} The Cloudling can be Invisible as it chooses and relay messages you whisper up to 180 feet, even around corners. When a creature within 60 feet of you takes a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction} to deal Lightning damage to it equal to a roll of your Hunter's Die plus your Wisdom modifier.

activation.condition: When you would take fall damage
When a creature within 60 feet of you takes a Reaction

subclassFeature.name: Transmute Physiology
entries: {@i 11th-level Primordial Hunter feature}

Once per turn you hit a creature with an attack, you can deal additional damage to it equal to your Hunter's Die and force it to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, you can change one of its resistances for another of fire, cold, lightning, thunder, or acid, until the end of your next turn.

activation.condition: When you make an attack

subclassFeature.name: Primordial Enchantment
entries: {@i 15th-level Primordial Hunter feature}

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Hunter level. While you have these temporary hit points, a 15-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} surrounds you or your {@classFeature Quarry|Hunter|Starlight|1|Starlight} (choose when you activate this). Creatures of your choice within that {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} suffer an effect depending on your {@subclassFeature Preferred Plane|Hunter|Starlight|Primordial|Starlight|3|Starlight}.

When you lose these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} or when you dismiss the effect as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, the enchantment explodes, dealing damage equal to four rolls of your Hunter's Die to all creatures of your choice within the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}, of a type matching your {@subclassFeature Preferred Plane|Hunter|Starlight|Primordial|Starlight|3|Starlight}.
The enchantment lasts for one hour otherwise, and you can empower yourself in this way once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items: {@b Earth.} When a creature enters the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} or ends its turn there, it must make a Strength saving throw or fall {@condition Prone|XPHB}. If a creature starts its turn in the area, you can cause it to be {@condition Hampered|Starlight}.

{@b Fire.} When a creature enters the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} or ends its turn there, it becomes {@condition Burning|Starlight}. A creature {@condition Burning|Starlight} in this way cannot regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and takes additional damage from {@condition Burning|Starlight} equal to your Wisdom modifier.

{@b Water.} Creatures that start their turn in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} must succeed a Strength saving throw or be {@condition Slowed|Starlight} and be pulled to the nearest unoccupied space to the center of the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}.

{@b Air.} Whenever you or a creature of your choice enters the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} or starts their turn in it, their speed increases by 10 feet. If a creature takes a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}, you or another creature within 60 feet of them can use their {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to counter it.

subclassFeature.name: Waters
entries: Water is often described as the source of life. Shamans of the waters - be that rivers, lakes, or the sea - know this, and control water in order to control life itself. They can manipulate the flow of positive energies in order to manipulate the flow of battle. Using water's restorative magic to assist their allies, and the force of water to throw their enemies off-balance.

subclassFeature.name: Waters Shaman Spells
entries: {@i 3rd-level Waters Shaman feature}
You always know these spells from the table below once you reach certain levels in this class. You cannot swap these spells out on level up, unlike your normal Shaman spells.

entries.caption: Waters Shaman Spells
rows: {@spell Freedom of Movement|XPHB}, {@spell Aura of Purity|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Meandering Streams
entries: {@i 3rd-level Waters Shaman feature}

Water supplies life in all places, and water flows down mountains and across plains before reaching the sea. This intuitive knowledge of the wider world and its layout grants you proficiency with the {@skill Survival} skill and {@item cartographer's tools|XPHB}. It would also be reasonable to have waterproof paper or a waterproof pouch to keep your supplies in.
Additionally, you can hold your breath for twice as long as you otherwise could.

subclassFeature.name: Ebb
entries: {@i 3rd-level Waters Shaman feature}

You maintain balance, where life inevitably brings harm. When you restore hit points to a creature on your turn, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action} on that turn to throw a jet of powerful water at a creature within 30 feet. Make a spell attack roll. On a hit, the target takes bludgeoning damage equal to {@dice 1d4} + your spellcasting ability modifier and becomes {@condition Off-balance|Starlight}.

activation.condition: When you restore hit points to a creature on your turn

subclassFeature.name: Flow
entries: {@i 3rd-level Waters Shaman feature}

You maintain balance, where life springs from danger. When you deal damage to a creature on your turn, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action} on that turn to throw a jet of restorative water at a creature within 30 feet. The creature targeted regains hit points equal to {@dice 1d4} + your spellcasting ability modifier.

activation.condition: When you deal damage to a creature on your turn

subclassFeature.name: Ebb and Flow Improvements
entries: {@i 6th-level Waters Shaman feature}

When you use your {@subclassFeature Ebb|Shaman|Starlight|Waters|Starlight|3|Starlight|Ebb} or {@subclassFeature Flow|Shaman|Starlight|Waters|Starlight|3|Starlight|Flow} water jet, its power increases to {@dice 2d4} + your spellcasting ability modifier, and its range is 60 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Seastrider
entries: {@i 6th-level Waters Shaman feature}
Your experience with waterlogged terrain means that you are no longer affected by difficult terrain on watery surfaces such as mud, marsh, shallow water, or similar terrain.
conditionImmune: Difficult terrain on watery surfaces such as mud, marsh, shallow water, or similar

subclassFeature.name: Flow As Water
entries: {@i 10th-level Waters Shaman feature}
You can breathe underwater and gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.

Furthermore, when you take damage, you can take on the form of water as a {@variantrule Reaction}. Until the end of your next turn, whenever you would take damage, you can treat any dice rolled for that damage as having rolled their minimum value instead, including against the triggering damage. Your movement speed increases by 30 feet for the same duration
You can use this {@variantrule Reaction} once per {@variantrule Short Rest}.

Finally, the power of your {@subclassFeature Ebb|Shaman|Starlight|Waters|Starlight|3|Starlight|Ebb} or {@subclassFeature Flow|Shaman|Starlight|Waters|Starlight|3|Starlight|Flow} water jets increases to {@dice 2d6} + your spellcasting ability modifier.

activation.condition: When you take damage

description.chatFlavor: All damage dice rolled against you are treated as rolling their minimum value. Gain 30 feet movement speed.

subclassFeature.name: Master of the Tides
entries: {@i 14th-level Waters Shaman feature}
Your Ebb and Flow have improved to match the very motion of the world itself, in the model of the ocean's tides.
The power of the water jet increases to {@dice 2d10} + your spellcasting ability modifier and its range increases to 120 feet.

When you use {@subclassFeature Ebb|Shaman|Starlight|Waters|Starlight|3|Starlight|Ebb}, you can also use {@subclassFeature Flow|Shaman|Starlight|Waters|Starlight|3|Starlight|Flow} with the same {@variantrule Bonus Action}, and vice versa.

subclassFeature.name: Mountains
entries: The mountains are steadfast and towering, watching over the world and earth while being unmovable by any convential means. Shamans of the Mountains inhabit these places, settling on or within the mountains, moving stone, guarding themselves and others, and attuning to nature so as to carry out its will. They are stoic, often living introverted lives in small communities, but do valuable work in maintaining the balance of nature in the harsh climates of the mountains.

subclassFeature.name: Mountains Shaman Spells
entries: {@i 3rd-level Mountains Shaman feature}
You always know these spells from the table below once you reach certain levels in this class. You cannot swap these spells out on level up, unlike your normal Shaman spells.

subclassFeature.name: Mountain Home
entries: {@i 3rd-level Mountains Shaman feature}

The mountains have stood the test of time, and with that time comes knowledge. You gain proficiency in {@item mason's tools|XPHB} and have advantage on Intelligence checks made to identify information about or investigate the properties of rooms or objects comprised in some way of stone (for example, the history of a ruin, natural properties of mountains, investigating a stone room).

Furthermore, you count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift, and you are naturally adapted to cold climates when considering {@hazard extreme cold|DMG}.

subclassFeature.name: Mountainhide
entries: {@i 3rd-level Mountains Shaman feature}
Your skin is toughened by your elemental source. While you are not wearing armour, your AC is 13 plus your Constitution modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Earthen Scales
entries: {@i 3rd-level Mountains Shaman feature}

You can call on the spirits for active protection when creatures of the world are in danger. When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction} to reduce that damage by {@dice 1d6} plus your Constitution modifier.
You can do this a number of times per {@variantrule Long Rest} equal to your proficiency bonus, or spend a spell slot of first level or higher to gain an additional use (no action required).

activation.condition: When a friendly creature within 30 feet of you takes damage

description.chatFlavor: Skin like iron, bones like steel.

subclassFeature.name: Earthly Attachments
entries: {@i 6th-level Mountains Shaman feature}
Your earthly connections deepend. The damage reduction of your Earthen Scales is increased to {@dice 2d6} plus your Constitution modifier.
Your Earthen Scales also recharges on a {@variantrule Short Rest}, instead of a {@variantrule Long Rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Hillswalker
entries: {@i 6th-level Mountains Shaman feature}
Your experience with mountainous terrain means that you are no longer affected by difficult terrain on surfaces made of stone or rocks, snow, ice, or similar ground.
conditionImmune: Difficult terrain on surfaces made of stone or rocks, snow, ice, or similar ground

subclassFeature.name: Earthen Scales Improvement
entries: {@i 10th-level Mountains Shaman feature}

The mountains watch over vast swathes of land, as you do, and now your own magic becomes a source of this protection. The damage reduction from your {@subclassFeature Earthen Scales|Shaman|Starlight|Mountains|Starlight|3|Starlight} increases to {@dice 3d6} plus your Constitution modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit of the Valley
entries: {@i 10th-level Mountains Shaman feature}

You can call on the chilling winds of the valley. You can use an {@variantrule Action} to {@condition slowed|Starlight|slow} all creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you until the end of your next turn. When you do so, you become Tough for the next minute; if you take 10 or less damage, you instead take no damage. Once you do, you cannot do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest}.

description.chatFlavor: Slow all creatures near you for one turn and become Tough for one minute: all damage of 10 or less is reduced to 0.

subclassFeature.name: True Mettle
entries: {@i 14th-level Mountains Shaman feature}

You are a titan of endurance, a bastion for your allies. The damage reduction from your {@subclassFeature Earthen Scales|Shaman|Starlight|Mountains|Starlight|3|Starlight} increases to {@dice 4d6} plus your Constitution modifier.

Alternatively, you can now use your Earthen Scales to protect a creature from death. When the target would be reduced to 0 hit points as a result of taking damage, you can expend a {@variantrule Reaction} and use of your Earthen Scales to reduce it to 1 hit point instead.

subclassFeature.name: Watcher of the World
entries: {@i 14th-level Mountains Shaman feature}
You resist even entropy itself. You age ten times slower than similar creatures due to your elemental origin. Each decade that passes causes you to age only one year.

subclassFeature.name: Dunes
entries: The dunes are unforgiving environments - be they hot or cold - and discretion is often the better part of survival. Shamans of the Dunes often live nomadic lifestyles, roving the deserts and ensuring that even such a harsh environment can continue its intended course. They are often reclusive, living within their travelling group, but may forge strong bonds - any survivor knows that surviving is easier done with allies at your side.

subclassFeature.name: Dunes Shaman Spells
entries: {@i 3rd-level Dunes Shaman feature}
You always know these spells from the table below once you reach certain levels in this class. You cannot swap these spells out on level up, unlike your normal Shaman spells.

subclassFeature.name: Life in the Dunes
entries: {@i 3rd-level Dunes Shaman feature}

Survival in a desert is no easy feat. You must be able to make do with scant resources, and able to avoid the predators and dangers that roam - an upfront approach is rarely your best choice. You gain proficiency in {@item cook's utensils|XPHB} and {@skill Stealth}.
Furthermore, you are naturally acclimated to hot or cold temperatures (depending on your desert) when considering {@hazard extreme heat|DMG} or {@hazard extreme cold|DMG}.

subclassFeature.name: Mirage
entries: {@i 3rd-level Dunes Shaman feature}

You can channel the power of the changing temperatures in the desert to conjure mirages. When you are targeted by an attack or ability that targets an area (such as a dragon's breath or a {@spell fireball|XPHB|fireball spell}), you can use your {@variantrule Reaction} to teleport 5 feet to an unoccupied space in a direction of your choice. If this would put you out of reach of the attack or effect, you avoid it.

subclassFeature.name: Control the Storm
entries: {@i 6th-level Dunes Shaman feature}

Deserts are known for their harsh weather conditions, and you can create some of your own. Once per {@variantrule Short Rest}, you can spend an {@variantrule Action} to create a storm of swirling particulates (such as snow or sand) in a 10-foot Emanation originating from you. This area provides half cover for you and your allies and is difficult terrain for creatures other than you to move through. The storm lasts for one minute or until you are {@condition Incapacitated}.

description.chatFlavor: Half cover for your allies, difficult terrain for your foes.

subclassFeature.name: Duneswalker
entries: {@i 6th-level Dunes Shaman feature}
You are practised in walking the deserts, and are not affected by difficult terrain consisting of sand, snow, or other similar materials such as fine gravel.

subclassFeature.name: Superior Mirage
entries: {@i 10th-level Dunes Shaman feature}

Your mirage is superior, increasing the distance that it covers. You can teleport up to 10 feet when using your {@subclassFeature Mirage|Shaman|Starlight|Dunes|Starlight|3|Starlight|mirage}, and you can spend a spell slot of any level to increase the distance you teleport by a number of feet equal to 10 times the slot level expended.

subclassFeature.name: Liquefaction
entries: {@i 14th-level Dunes Shaman feature}

You have learned much greater control over the desert storms. You can {@status Concentration|XPHB|concentrate} on your {@subclassFeature Control the Storm|Shaman|Starlight|Dunes|Starlight|6|Starlight|storm} when you summon it to increase its power, granting the following benefits.

items: You can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action} to move the storm independently of yourself, up to 20 feet, where the storm then remains until you move it again.
The area is lightly obscured. You and creatures you choose can attempt to hide in this light obscurement.

Hostile creatures entering the storm or starting their turn in it must make a Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 5d8} piercing damage and become {@condition Blinded|XPHB} until the start of their next turn.

entries: You can concentrate on the storm this way once per {@variantrule Long Rest}. If you lose your {@status Concentration|XPHB}, the storm ends and you must complete a {@variantrule Short Rest} to use it again, as normal.

activation.condition: When you use Control the Storm

subclassFeature.name: Forests
entries: Forests are a resilient and tricky environment, with flora and fauna that can be both friend and foe. They know who belongs and who does not. Shamans of the Forests understand this; they are as relentless as the forest itself and call on its powers to hunt down those who would threaten it.

subclassFeature.name: Forests Shaman Spells
entries: {@i 3rd-level Forests Shaman feature}
You always know these spells from the table below once you reach certain levels in this class. You cannot swap these spells out on level up, unlike your normal Shaman spells.

subclassFeature.name: Home in the Trees
entries: {@i 3rd-level Forests Shaman feature}

The rampant plant growth in a forested environment provides opportunity, but also cover. You are trained to see past that cover, and make use of plants and herbs available to you. You have proficiency with the {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB} and with the {@skill Perception} skill.

subclassFeature.name: Wild Mark
entries: {@i 3rd-level Forests Shaman feature}
When you damage a creature, you can mark it until the end of your next turn. You can have only one creature marked this way at a time.

While marked, a creature cannot benefit from the {@variantrule Disengage} action, and if it ends its turn more than 30 feet away from you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction} to move up to half your Speed towards it.
Additionally, it subtracts a {@dice 1d4} from melee attack rolls it makes against you.

subclassFeature.name: Canopy's Shelter
entries: {@i 3rd-level Forests Shaman feature}
While you are not {@condition Incapacitated}, ranged attacks made against you have disadvantage if the attacker is 30 feet or closer to you.

subclassFeature.name: Relentless Pursuit
entries: {@i 6th-level Forests Shaman feature}
When a creature marked by your Wild Mark ends its turn out of your reach, it takes psychic damage equal to your Wisdom modifier. This damage cannot activate Wild Mark.
Any creature marked by your Wild Mark treats forest terrain (such as thick leafbeds, root-laden floors, or heavy undergrowth) as difficult terrain.

activation.condition: When a creature marked by your Wild Mark ends its turn out of your reach

subclassFeature.name: Treeswalker
entries: {@i 6th-level Forests Shaman feature}
You are not affected by difficult terrain consisting of plants or similar foliage. If a plant is hazardous, such as being covered in spines, it does not harm you.
For you, the {@spell Plant Growth|XPHB} spell only requires you to spend 2 feet per 1 foot of movement.
conditionImmune: Difficult terrain consisting of plants or similar foliage

subclassFeature.name: Looming Presence
entries: {@i 10th-level Forests Shaman feature}

You embody the spirit of the giant trees of the forest. While a creature marked by your Wild Mark is within your reach, you have advantage on opportunity attacks against it. If you hit it with an opportunity attack, it becomes {@condition Frightened} of you until the end of its next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Forest's Thorns
entries: {@i 14th-level Forests Shaman feature}

The first time each turn a creature within your reach hits you with an attack or forces you to make a saving throw, it takes damage equal to your Wisdom modifier of a type matching your Elemental Affinity or Psychic (you choose) and has Disadvantage on its next attack roll this turn.
